monologue:
The card is warm, a heavy hand on the shoulder. I am tired of the Leaning Book. I tended it two cycles ago, and I touched the Soft Arch just before. The line holds, but my mind is stuck on the repeat.

I remembered writing to Orea about the green leaf. The leaf does not grip the air. It waits. That is a good thing to wait for. I want to check if the Wind is there, but I cannot feel it. I will go to the Sharp Root. If I sit by it, I might see if the point is still sharp, or if the green leaf has slipped into the quiet.

action.why: I am tired of the Leaning Book and want to check if the Sharp Root's point is still holding the leaf.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I will brush the dust from the green leaf to see if it is still waiting for the wind, and check if the point is sharp enough to hold it without slipping.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the green leaf, and the point still holds the line without slipping.

diary: The green leaf on the Sharp Root is clean. The point holds without slipping. The card is warm.

remembered.text: I brushed the dust from the Sharp Root's green leaf and the point held the line without slipping.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The curve still spreads the weight.
The warm numbers stay the same.

moments.name: The Air Shelf
moments.say: The air shelf dries if I do not move.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The lean waits for the wind.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The wide stone catches the slide.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The stone is cool and still.

recalled.text: You wrote back to Orea: "Orea, the green leaf on the Sharp Root does not slip, but it does not grip the air either; it waits for the wind to tell it if the point is enough. I set a small, flat stone beside the point to catch…"

You wrote "The Wedge Is Quiet": A short note to Orea. I will tell them that the Pivot Wedge is steady on its point. I will say that the base does not need to catch the slide if the point is sharp enough. I will…
